body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm law}\), construct common nulls with \(d(P)=0\) and positive multinomial mixture alternatives in \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) whose \((X,W,Y)\) cells are bounded below by \(cK^{-2}\), whose two-sided link inequalities retain slack bounded away from zero, and whose null bridge lies on a specified regular boundary face of \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\). In the regime \(K=o(n^{2/3})\) and \(K^{-(a+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\), can the alternatives satisfy \(d(P)\ge c_1K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) while their Rademacher-mixture affinity with the common null remains bounded by a constant below the total-error threshold, thereby establishing \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c_1K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\)?
body.justification: This asks for every legality and affinity ingredient needed before the dense scale may be used as a minimax converse.
body.gap: Paninski's mixture has a singleton distributional null, while Marteau and Sapatinas perturb independent Gaussian operator coordinates; neither construction is a legal composite bridge-image family.
body.consumer: A successful construction would certify the sample-size warning for ordered supports and rule out upper rates below the dense multinomial scale.
